notes.title: August 2025 Monthly Update
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44791682/33c7e6cd57c622808ff0910b168f0bc35735c98e.gif"]

The August 2025 update for Typing Simulator is now live!

We're now into the second of these monthly updates. This will be the first of the visual content additions to the game with a new wood keycap shader! Wooden keycaps are a pretty popular alternative material, so we wanted to do our best to take the time to capture the look of these accurately. All of our keycap materials use one main monolithic shader, so the upgrades that we made for the wood material will also improve our preexisting materials. Even without the wood shader you'll see some (potentially very subtle, but still present) improvements in the visuals of your current keebs too. 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44791682/2c45ba992dc12c68e75385e17f149e7e6df38074.jpg"]

For those more interested in the technical side of things: the main change to the shader that allowed for the wood material to happen was us spinning up a custom triplanar texture effect with per axis texture tiling. While all of the keycaps are UVed pretty meticulously (we'll have to do a whole separate blog post about this at some point), using a triplanar effect for this allowed us to get where we wanted to be without making those keycap UVs even more complicated.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44791682/39e9fecf9e42d4f1c4e26d4ff0ef566aa4c0f7af.png"](This doesn't even include the multiple subgraphs!)



This also gave us the chance to find a sneaky bug in the keyboard initialization script. If you ever saw your keycap textures jump around kind of randomly, or ever had all of the textures look exactly the same accross all of your keycaps, that should be fixed now. This won't be our last pass at shader improvements (as it most certainly isn't going to be the only material we add, we have a few more in the works!), so you should see even more of these sorts of upgrades soon.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44791682/1514940f3e273c8f376a6006dcb963ef67477989.gif"]

(Yeah, these gifs are rough, but they look cool!)



Aside from this, you should see some more UI improvements. We've upgraded the look on the Control Hint UI by redoing the visuals a little bit and adding some more sleek animations. That had been stubbed in real quick along the way and we hadn't made time to go back and refresh that till now, so it had been looking a little rough. While this in of itself isn't a crazy impactful change, it lays the groundwork for all of the UI to hit a new level of polish as we go along.

Thank you yet again for all of the support, let us know if you encounter any bugs, and we'll keep the content coming your way!

Typing Simulator Dev Team

notes.title: July 2025 Monthly Update
notes.content:
Hey there everybody! We've been officially in early access for a few weeks now! It has been a blast to be able to see you all get into the game and give us a bunch of great feedback. All of the bug reports have been super helpful as well, thank you all for that. We want to keep the ball rolling, so this will be the beginning of us doing monthly feature releases moving forward. We'll still get to any bug fixes asap, we're just going to keep the rest of the updates to one big monthly push.

As this was the beginning of our early access journey, we did spend a bunch of our time clearing out the initial wave of bug reports. We still have some quality of life upgrades to send your way though!

Added new icon for workshop mode

Added locked icons to the currently locked game modes to make the status extra clear

Added 12 more achievements to fill out the newer game modes (we're now up from 19 to 31!)

Holding ALT in the workshop while in 2D mode now shows a top down view of the keyboard to make viewing your work in progress easier

Filtered out apostrophes from capital letter drills to balance out difficulty

We have a bunch more things coming down the pipe for you but those will start rolling out in the coming monthly updates. And this way we can say that the reason we're no where near the top of the leaderboards is totally cause we're too busy working on things and not because we can't keep up. Totally.



Thanks again!

Typing Simulator Dev Team

notes.title: Demo Update: Interval Mode
notes.content:
We have been cooking up a few new game modes, and have decided to drop one into the demo for everyone to try out!

Interval Mode is like our version of an endless mode, where you progress through harder and harder phrases against a set timer. Completing a phrase earns you extra time (with an extra bonus for a perfect phrase), and highlighted words will earn you bonus time on top of that if you can get through them without any errors. Work your way through as many levels you can before time is up, and see where that lands you on the leaderboards! This already proved fairly competitive in our playtesting, but Nathan was wrecking the rest of the dev team a little too hard. We're adding this in to the demo so that we can get the boards a little more full and have someone actually put up a fight!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44791682/ec85c9750e1224bcf6a9d6107910fd1281bb9121.gif

Please give it a shot and let us know what you think so far!

Typing Simulator Dev Team
